eyebrow: Eat Like a Local in Chanthaburi · Updated 2026
intro: Chanthaburi is a city where local food is still the real thing. From moo cha muang — that triple-note sour-sweet-salty pork — to sen chan pad poo with its uniquely springy noodles you simply can't replicate elsewhere, we've pulled together 10 places that locals actually eat at and that visitors never regret. It spans old-town heritage eateries, century-old kuayteow liang, fresh seafood at Kung Wiman and Tha Chaleb, and waterfront cafes along the Chanthaboon riverside strip.
chips: 🦀 Sen chan pad poo — crab-fried noodles

blocks.html:
Chanthaburi takes food more seriously than most people expect. The magic is in local dishes still made the traditional way — moo cha muang, where the perfect sour-sweet-salty balance comes from fresh cha muang leaves; sen chan pad poo, with its distinctively chewy noodles tossed with crabmeat; and kuayteow liang, whose broth is scented with "rew" (a rare galangal-family herb) in a way no other place can replicate. Stroll the Chanthaboon Riverside community in the old town and you'll find one heritage shop after another. Drive out toward Kung Wiman or Tha Chaleb and the seafood is so fresh it's practically still swimming. Back in the city center there are cafes and riverside restaurants for a relaxing evening. One city, every flavor.

Many places on this list are long-standing institutions. Chanthorn Restaurant has been open since 1962 and remains the first name people mention when Chanthaburi food comes up. Krua Maneechan is the hotel restaurant that reviewers consistently rank at the top of the province. Kuayteow Liang Pa Tid at Tha Mai is said to hold a recipe that has been passed down for nearly a century. Puja Tha Chaleb has been selling seafood for more than forty years. And Baan Namprik Khao Suay arranges its local-style set meals so beautifully they have become the defining image of Chanthaburi home food. Any of them is the genuine article — mark them on the map and go taste them all.

blocks.name: Krua Maneechan
blocks.signature: Moo cha muang, sen chan pad poo, pla tom krawan, yam mangkut
blocks.descHtml:
If you arrive in Chanthaburi and want authentic local food in a comfortable setting, Krua Maneechan is likely the first name a local will mention. The restaurant belongs to Maneechan Resort and has been open for over 40 years — it has essentially become a culinary landmark of the city. A great first meal for new arrivals, or for families and groups who want to order a spread and share. The resort grounds are lush and shaded, the dining room is airy, service is attentive, and multiple reviews note that staff are happy to guide you through the menu.

The dish you must order is moo cha muang — the signature of Chanthaburi. Pork braised to tender, with a beautifully balanced sour-sweet flavor from fresh cha muang leaves. Reviewers consistently call it outstanding. The next essential is soft crab sen chan pad poo: springy noodles stir-fried with generous crabmeat — a signature dish you can't leave without trying. For bold flavors, the pla tom krawan (fish simmered with cardamom herb) is intensely aromatic, and the yam mangkut (mangosteen salad) adds a bright sour-sweet freshness from seasonal fruit. Beyond those, standouts include yam poo khai dong (marinated crab roe salad), Maneechan sausage, and som tum durian — nearly impossible to find elsewhere.

Prices sit at the hotel-restaurant level, roughly 251–500 THB per person; seafood and crab-heavy orders can push a bit higher. For the freshness and ingredient quality, it's fair value. The restaurant opens every day from around 06:30 through to the evening, covering breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Whether you're stopping in on your way through or staying at the resort, it works for any meal.

One thing to know: some local-ingredient dishes follow the seasons — especially yam mangkut and som tum durian. If you're set on a specific dish, call ahead to confirm availability. During holidays the restaurant fills up, so booking a table or arriving a little early makes things easier.
mustOrder: Soft crab sen chan pad poo
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province / family groups

blocks.name: Chanthorn Restaurant (Maharaj Branch)
blocks.area: Maharaj Road, Mueang Chanthaburi District, Chanthaburi
blocks.signature: Gaeng moo cha muang, sen chan pad poo, pla tom rakam sai krawan, moo kapi wan
blocks.descHtml:
For authentic Chanthaburi local food, Chanthorn Restaurant — Maharaj Branch — is the place both locals and travelers mention most. It has been a fixture of the city for over 50 years and received the Shell Chuan Chim award in the early days of the program. This branch sits on Maharaj Road in the old town, decorated as a traditional Thai house, warm and family-style — for anyone who wants genuinely local flavors, not run-of-the-mill Thai food.

The must-order is gaeng moo cha muang — pork belly braised until tender in a rounded, sour broth made with cha muang leaves in a way you will rarely find outside Chanthaburi. Another regular pairing is sen chan pad poo: springy noodles wok-fried with fresh crabmeat, well-balanced flavor. For something different, try the moo kapi wan (sweet shrimp-paste pork) or pla tom rakam sai krawan, with its distinctive sour-aromatic profile. Nam prik fans should try the sarang wa and loma chu — old-school recipes from this kitchen.

Most reviewers praise the bold, well-seasoned flavors, fresh ingredients, and genuinely local character. A few note that prices have nudged up over the years and the restaurant has no air conditioning, so midday can feel warm — but the majority agree it is worth it. Per-person spend runs around 250–500 THB for a multi-dish spread; the gaeng moo cha muang is around 279 THB and the sen chan pad poo around 129 THB.

Open every day around 10:00–20:00 (kitchen closes around 20:30). Parking is available and extra spaces are added on holidays. Come at a relaxed time if you can — busy especially on weekends. For souvenirs, canned gaeng moo cha muang and local products are available to take home. For a first meal in Chanthaburi, this is the safest, most complete choice.
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province, authentic Chanthaburi local food
blocks.spice: Medium (some dishes are bold and intense)

blocks.name: Jae Pen Yen Ta Fo Poo Kang Wat Phai Lom
blocks.signature: Yen ta fo poo kang ruam mit (soup/dry), fried tofu
blocks.descHtml:
Ask any Chanthaburi local which yen ta fo shop to try first and Jae Pen Yen Ta Fo Poo Kang Wat Phai Lom will come up immediately. This is the original — located near Wat Phai Lom for several decades, a landmark that both locals and travelers make a point of visiting. The shop's defining feature is right there in the name: yen ta fo loaded with whole mud crab and mantis shrimp. For anyone who wants serious seafood noodles rather than a standard fishball bowl, this is the place.

The must-order is the yen ta fo poo kang ruam mit — available in soup or dry versions. The broth has the classic yen ta fo pink hue with a rounded sour-sweet flavor. The mantis shrimp and crab meat draw consistent praise from reviewers: fresh, without any fishiness, with a firm, bouncy texture. Multiple sizes are available for those who want extra toppings. The other item not to skip is the fried tofu — fresh out of the oil, crispy outside, soft inside, served with the house dipping sauce. Nearly every table orders it as a side.

Pricing: plain yen ta fo starts around 60 THB; with crab it moves to around 100 THB; the full loaded version runs about 150 THB and up depending on size. Fried tofu is about 45 THB per plate. Average spend per person: 100–250 THB — fair for the amount of seafood you get. The shophouse setting is simple, no air conditioning; if the inside is full there are tables across the way. Parking is easy in the temple lot.

Open daily from around 08:00–16:00. Come in the morning through early afternoon, as popular items can sell out. The kitchen prioritizes freshness so the queue moves during busy periods. Yen ta fo this good — with genuinely fresh crab and mantis shrimp — is exactly why people keep returning generation after generation.
mustOrder: Yen ta fo poo kang ruam mit (soup)
tags: Yen ta fo with crab and mantis shrimp
blocks.spice: Adjustable (the broth is sour-sweet, not spicy)

blocks.name: Kuayteow Liang Pa Tid Tha Mai
blocks.signature: Kuayteow moo liang, nuea liang (herb broth with rew), khanom thuai
blocks.descHtml:
Kuayteow Liang Pa Tid Tha Mai is one of those legendary spots where any conversation about Chanthaburi's kuayteow liang begins. The shop has been a fixture at the old Tha Mai market for nearly a century, occupying a classic wooden shophouse on Rachakij Road, across from the Tha Mai branch of the Government Savings Bank. What draws people from far away is the word "liang" — a local-style herbed broth that uses "rew," a rare galangal-family herb that gives the stock an aromatic complexity no other kitchen can duplicate. For anyone who wants the real, hyper-local food of Chanthaburi rather than standard noodles, this is it.

The must-orders are the kuayteow moo liang and nuea liang — pork or beef, your choice. The beef is thinly sliced, tender, with no gamey edge, packed into the bowl with soft liver. Reviewers consistently note that the broth tastes sweet and gentle because the kitchen uses cane sugar rather than refined sugar — good enough to finish straight, without adding condiments. A squeeze of the house-made sour orange nam prik brightens the whole bowl instantly. Finish with khanom thuai (small coconut-milk steamed cups), mildly sweet and creamy. Prices are remarkably wallet-friendly.

Pricing: a bowl starts at 50 THB, special at 70 THB; khanom thuai is just a few baht each; som mapeed (sour lime juice) is 20 THB a glass. The setting is a spacious old wooden house with tables arranged inside — a steady flow of regulars all day. Open daily around 09:00–15:00; mornings to early afternoon only.

The kitchen sells out fast on busy days, so arriving before noon gives you the best selection with no queue. Street parking is available along the market strip. If you're driving the Chanthaburi–Tha Mai road, stop for a bowl and you'll understand why this place has been here for nearly a century.
blocks.bestFor: Breakfast or lunch, authentic local Chanthaburi food

blocks.name: Puja Tha Chaleb
blocks.area: Tha Chaleb Road, Bang Kacha Sub-district, Mueang Chanthaburi District, Chanthaburi
blocks.signature: Puja (stuffed crab), khao pad poo, grilled tiger prawns, sour curry with fish roe
blocks.descHtml:
If you want fresh seafood that the locals trust, Puja Tha Chaleb is one of the first names you'll hear. The restaurant has anchored the Tha Chaleb neighborhood for over 40 years, growing from a modest riverside shed into a spacious dining room that seats close to two hundred, with both air-conditioned sections and open-air zones. Perfect for families bringing grandparents, or large groups who want to order a full spread of Thai seafood dishes. Wide parking — no hunting for a spot.

The dish you cannot miss is the puja itself — crab meat mixed with minced pork, stuffed back into the shell, then deep-fried until fragrant. Genuinely delicious. Follow with khao pad poo (crab fried rice) loaded with crabmeat, whole grilled tiger prawns with firm sweet flesh, and sour curry with fish roe that pairs perfectly with steamed rice. Steamed sea crab and swimming crab are both available. Reviewers consistently describe the crab meat as fresh, firm, and naturally sweet. Stir-fried squid with salted egg yolk and deep-fried sea bass with fish sauce are popular repeat orders.

Pricing is fair for the quality and freshness — roughly 251–500 THB per person; ordering whole crabs by the kilo adjusts the cost upward. The restaurant takes credit cards, has plenty of seating, and there's a Puja Cafe at the entrance for coffee after your meal. The location is about 10 km from the city center along Tha Chaleb Road, set among shady mangroves. Open daily around 10:00–22:00 (kitchen starts closing around 21:00). Come mid-morning or before the evening peak for the freshest selection and shorter waits.

During long holidays and festivals, tour buses sometimes arrive in numbers, which can slow service and stretch wait times. Large groups should call ahead to reserve. Overall this is a seafood restaurant that rarely disappoints — which is why it has held the trust of both locals and visitors for so many decades.
blocks.spice: Medium (curries and salads can be made spicy)

blocks.name: Baan Namprik Khao Suay
blocks.signature: Traditional namprik-khao suay set meal, khanom jeen chao chan, khao ho nakrop
blocks.descHtml:
Baan Namprik Khao Suay is the Chanthaburi local-food restaurant that many people put on their must-visit-once list for the city. It started with two women: Mae Id, whose family nam prik recipes have been handed down through generations, and her daughter, who returned home to rebrand the shop, redesign the space, and tell the story on social media until the whole province took notice. For anyone who wants genuine Chanthaburi food in a beautifully arranged set meal — so beautiful you almost hesitate to touch it — this place is a strong choice. Especially good for people who love nam prik and want to try the full range of local condiments in one sitting.

The dish people talk about most is the namprik-khao suay set arranged in the old style. The kitchen offers dozens of nam prik varieties — both classic recipes and new house creations — served alongside hot steamed rice, fried fish, fresh vegetables, and a full spread of accompaniments. Another popular set is the khanom jeen chao chan: rice noodles with all the local toppings, Chanthaburi-style. And khao ho nakrop is a banana-leaf-wrapped meal in the traditional style of this city. Beyond the sets, there are elegant snacks like miang kham on lotus petals, golden cups, dried watermelon fish, and local classics like moo cha muang and kai tom krawan.

Most reviewers praise the presentation — dishes are styled so beautifully that photographing them becomes half the experience — and the bold, thoroughly Thai flavor of the nam prik. Some reviews honestly note that certain dishes skew quite sour-forward; if you don't love sour flavors, look more carefully at which items suit you. The setting is a contemporary-traditional Thai space with comfortable seating, good for families or groups. Mid-range pricing; set meals start in the low hundreds and portions are generous, so the more people the better value.

Located in Mueang Chanthaburi District, open daily around 09:00–17:30. The restaurant has moved locations before, so check the latest address on the shop's page or Instagram before heading over. Groups visiting on long weekends should call ahead — the place fills up quickly and reserving a table is worth the effort.
blocks.bestFor: Lunch for local-food lovers, family or group meals
blocks.spice: Medium spice, adjustable; some dishes are sour-forward

blocks.name: Wiman Seafood by Pa Le
blocks.area: Kung Wiman Beach, Nayai Am District, Chanthaburi
blocks.signature: Shrimp marinated in fish sauce, sun-dried squid with roe, stir-fried scallops, sour curry with fish roe
blocks.descHtml:
Wiman Seafood by Pa Le is a beachside seafood restaurant at Kung Wiman, Nayai Am District, Chanthaburi — sitting directly on the water, across from Peggy Cove and close to Laem Sing. It's the kind of relaxed seaside dining spot that suits road-trippers who've come to Kung Wiman and want fresh seafood with a sea view. The kitchen's strength is the quality and size of the ingredients, especially the prawns. Wide tables accommodate families and larger groups comfortably.

The dishes that come up most in reviews are the shrimp marinated in fish sauce — large, firm-fleshed prawns; sun-dried squid with roe that has a rich, sweet egg flavor; stir-fried scallops with aromatic herbs; and sour curry with fish roe that goes perfectly with hot steamed rice. Beyond those, the menu extends to oyster omelette, steamed squid with lime, seafood with curry powder, glass-noodle baked prawns, and clear tom yam goong. A thorough spread of seafood dishes for a full table.

The atmosphere is open and breezy — the kind of seaside setting made for long, unhurried meals with a view. Pricing is typical for a seafood restaurant of this type: roughly 250–500 THB per person, depending on the menu and prawn sizes. Many regular visitors praise the freshness and atmosphere; a handful of reviews note that some dishes run a bit pricey and that not every plate hits the mark for every palate — normal variance for seafood restaurants where satisfaction often depends on what you order.

Before you go, confirm hours and book a table during long weekends, when Kung Wiman is at peak capacity. Ask about prawn and seafood prices by weight before ordering to plan your budget. Then grab a table at the water's edge for the full view.
blocks.bestFor: Seaside seafood meal with family or friends while visiting Kung Wiman
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: seafood · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.name: Jae Id Rimnam
blocks.area: Chanthaboon Riverside Community, Mueang Chanthaburi District, Chanthaburi
blocks.signature: Tom yam seafood noodles with crab and mantis shrimp, khao na seafood, khao ruam jao samut
blocks.descHtml:
If you're strolling the Chanthaboon Riverside community and wondering where to have lunch, Jae Id Rimnam is one of the most frequently recommended spots by both locals and visitors. It's an old-school seafood noodle shop in a traditional wooden shophouse right on the river, where the owner herself still cooks every bowl. For anyone who wants serious, genuinely fresh seafood noodles at a good price while absorbing old-town atmosphere, this is the address.

Everyone orders the tom yam seafood noodles. The star is the mantis shrimp and crab — generous, firm, and fresh. Reviewers consistently describe the broth as sharply sour, bold, fragrant with lemongrass, and packed with prawn, squid, and crab claw in a single bowl. If you'd rather skip the noodles, there's khao na seafood, khao ruam jao samut (mixed seafood rice), and other rice-plate options. Close with khanom thuai and som mapeed — the local sweet and local beverage — to round it out properly.

Noodle prices: around 100 THB, special at 120 THB; average per person around 100–250 THB — good value for the seafood you receive. The shop is on Sukhaphibal Road inside the Chanthaboon Riverside community: cross the bridge in front of the Catholic church and turn left a few metres. Open daily around 09:00–16:00. Google rating 3.9 stars, reflecting solid consensus on flavor and freshness.

The shop is small — under ten tables — no air conditioning, and packed around midday. Expect a queue and a wait, because the owner cooks each bowl individually. Coming before noon is easiest. No parking at the shop; park at the Catholic church and walk in. If you're patient, this bowl is worth every minute of the wait.
mustOrder: Tom yam seafood noodles with crab and mantis shrimp
blocks.bestFor: Seafood lunch in the old-town riverside neighborhood
blocks.spice: Bold tom yam spice (adjustable on request)
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: seafood · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.name: Dugo Space
blocks.signature: Slow-bar coffee, cocoa, art gallery and jewelry corner
blocks.descHtml:
Dugo Space is a slow-bar cafe tucked away in the gem-market district, Soi Krajang 4, Mueang Chanthaburi. Three things come together here in a way that actually works: quality coffee, a rotating art gallery, and a display of genuine Chanthaburi gemstones and jewelry. For people who lean toward art, prefer quiet and a dark-tone aesthetic, and want to sit with a good cup and look at something interesting, this is the spot. The interior runs a Black and Dark palette — cool but welcoming. Visitors often say it feels like stepping into a coffee studio belonging to a friend who loves art. Good photo angles on every level.

The coffee people talk about most is the slow-bar pour — the barista extracts each cup by hand, using a Thai-made extraction device on display in the shop. The flavor is intense and satisfying. For non-coffee drinkers, the hot cocoa and matcha latte both get strong reviews for smooth, mellow flavor. The peach tea also comes up — bright and refreshing with a sour-sweet edge. For something unexpected, try whichever house signature the barista recommends that day.

Pricing is friendly — Wongnai reviewers note a spend well under 100 THB per person for a quality cup, a stylish environment, and free access to the art and gem displays. The cafe sits right next to the Chanthaboon Riverside community and the gem-trading quarter, so it's easy to continue exploring after your drink. Open Tue–Sun approximately 09:00–17:00; closed Mondays.

This spot has developed a following among Chanthaburi cafe-goers because it packages coffee, a multi-story art gallery, and genuine gemstone jewelry in one venue — genuinely rare for a smaller city. The rotating art means something new each visit. Check opening hours on the shop's page before going, as times can shift slightly by day.
blocks.bestFor: Art and cafe lovers — sit with a coffee and browse the gallery

blocks.name: Tha Majun (Tamajun)
blocks.area: Sukhaphibal Road, Chanthaboon Riverside, Mueang Chanthaburi District, Chanthaburi
blocks.signature: Thai riverside food, retro atmosphere, live classical music in the evenings
blocks.descHtml:
If you want a place in Chanthaburi where you can eat well, hear good music, and get a riverside retro atmosphere all at once, Tha Majun is one of the most frequently cited spots among both locals and visitors. The restaurant sits in the old riverside community along the Chanthaboon river — a classic wooden house with tables extending over the water, an in-house cafe, and a small hotel upstairs. Great for couples, groups of friends, or families, especially for an evening meal when the vibe is at its best.

The dishes reviewers mention most consistently are local Chanthaburi classics — moo cha muang with its rounded sour flavor from cha muang leaves, and kai pad krawan (chicken stir-fried with cardamom) that carries an unmistakable local herb fragrance. Single-dish diners often go for khao pad kak moo, which reviewers say is satisfying without being greasy, and pad Thai sen chan with fresh prawns — a signature of this kitchen. For snacks with drinks, the pla kapong nam tok and hot cheese balls work well, or the yam kho moo yang that consistently sells out. A nice touch: some dishes arrive served in a tiered tiffin carrier, which has a charming Thai feel.

The real draw at Tha Majun is the atmosphere and the music. During the day it's easy and calm — good for a coffee and a relaxed sit. Come evening, a live band plays Thai songs from the 80s and 90s, drifting over the water like a relaxed, nostalgic venue you'd never want to leave. Most reviews single out the atmosphere and music as the highlight. Pricing runs around 101–250 THB per person — fair for a venue of this quality.

On weekdays the restaurant typically opens from the evening onwards; on weekends from midday. If the live music is the reason you're going, come for dinner. During peak season the place fills up, and a handful of reviews note that food can take a while and portions on certain dishes run small — allow some flexibility. Overall it's a place people return to for the combination of local food, riverside setting, and live music in one spot.
mustOrder: Pad Thai sen chan with fresh prawns

blocks.title: Know Before You Eat in Chanthaburi

items.title: Getting Around
items.text: Chanthaburi has no rail transit and Grab coverage is thin. Renting a car or motorbike is the most practical option, especially for the seaside spots at Kung Wiman and Tha Chaleb that sit outside the city. Within the old town and the Chanthaboon Riverside area, walking is easy.

items.title: Paying
items.text: Noodle shops, street food stalls, and smaller restaurants generally work on cash only. Some accept PromptPay (QR scan). Keep small bills and coins handy for the best experience. Larger restaurants and cafes may accept cards.

items.title: Avoiding Queues
items.text: Popular noodle and yen ta fo shops open in the morning and close in the afternoon — dishes often sell out before closing. Arrive before noon to get the full menu without queuing. On long weekends, local-food and seafood restaurants get very busy; avoid the midday lunch peak if you can.

items.title: About the Flavors
items.text: Local specialties like moo cha muang and kuayteow liang have distinct herb notes unique to Chanthaburi. If you prefer no spice, tell the kitchen — and try ordering the traditional version first so you taste what the restaurant intends.

items.title: Language and Menus
items.text: Smaller shops generally have Thai-only menus. English menus are not universal. Pointing at pictures, or showing a photo of the dish name, works well — locals here are friendly and patient.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: No tip expected at casual restaurants and street stalls. Larger restaurants with full table service often add a service charge. Leaving small change at a place where you enjoyed the meal is a welcome gesture.

blocks.title: Plan a Full Day of Eating in Chanthaburi
blocks.html:
Many local and noodle restaurants in Chanthaburi open at midday and close by late afternoon — Kuayteow Liang Pa Tid and Jae Id Rimnam both close around 15:00–16:00, and Jae Pen Yen Ta Fo Poo Kang closes mid-afternoon too. If you want to hit them all, start early and plan your midday meal around noodles or yen ta fo, then keep the places open into the evening — like Krua Maneechan or Chanthorn Restaurant — for dinner.

If you have a car, a half-day sea trip is worth planning: drive out to Kung Wiman for a meal at Wiman Seafood by Pa Le with the water right there, then circle back into the old town for a walk through the Chanthaboon Riverside community. Stop at Jae Id Rimnam or sit with a slow-bar coffee at Dugo Space, and close the evening with dinner by the river at Tha Majun with live music. A clean timeline for one day.

blocks.text: Come to Chanthaburi without a return deadline — book a night in the city center or by the sea and eat from morning to night.

faq.q: Which restaurant in Chanthaburi is the most famous?
faq.a: For local cuisine, Chanthorn Restaurant is the first name that comes up — open since 1962 and now a city institution. Krua Maneechan is the hotel restaurant that reviewers consistently rank at the top of the province. Both are known for moo cha muang and sen chan pad poo.

faq.q: What are the signature foods of Chanthaburi?
faq.a: The local dishes you must try are moo cha muang (a sour-sweet-salty pork braise from cha muang leaves), sen chan pad poo (springy rice noodles stir-fried with crab), kuayteow liang (herb-infused noodle soup with rew from Tha Mai), and yen ta fo poo kang with firm-flesh crab and mantis shrimp. During fruit season, yam mangkut (mangosteen salad) is also worth trying.

faq.q: How much does a meal in Chanthaburi cost?
faq.a: Noodles and yen ta fo run roughly 50–150 THB per bowl — Kuayteow Liang Pa Tid starts around 50–70 THB. Local Thai restaurants like Krua Maneechan and Chanthorn Restaurant, plus seafood spots, generally come to 250–500 THB per person depending on what you order. At a cafe like Dugo Space, drinks run about 60–100 THB.

faq.q: Do I need to book a table at the popular restaurants?
faq.a: Noodle and street-food places generally don't require reservations — just walk in. During long weekends or fruit season when visitor numbers spike, local restaurants and seafood spots like Wiman Seafood by Pa Le and Puja Tha Chaleb can get very busy. Calling ahead or arriving before the peak hours makes it easier.

faq.q: Which restaurants in Chanthaburi are open late into the evening?
faq.a: Several local restaurants stay open through the evening: Krua Maneechan is open until around 23:00. The riverside Tha Majun runs until midnight with live music. Puja Tha Chaleb's kitchen serves until around 21:00. Kuayteow Liang Pa Tid, Jae Id Rimnam, and Jae Pen Yen Ta Fo Poo Kang are daytime-only spots that close around mid-afternoon — go early.
